literal: In the twenty-first year, the emperor died.
idiomatic: Year twenty-one: the emperor died.

literal: In the first Long’an year, Wang Gong, Yin Zhongkan, Huan Xuan, and others together raised troops, memorializing in the name of executing Wang Guobao.
idiomatic: Long’an one: Wang Gong, Yin Zhongkan, Huan Xuan, and allies mobilized to kill Wang Guobao.

literal: The court yielded and killed him, also beheading his cousin Xu; Sima Daozi thereby lost power, and disaster and rebellion were accomplished.
idiomatic: The court complied, executed Guobao and Wang Xu, leaving Sima Daozi broken as chaos set in.

literal: In the eighteenth year’s second month, a guest star was inside the Tail, lasting until the ninth month before it was extinguished.
idiomatic: Year eighteen, February–September: a guest star lingered in the Tail.

literal: The prognostication states: "Yan will have arms and mourning."
idiomatic: Yan lands face war and death.

literal: In the twentieth year, Murong Chui’s son Bao campaigned against Wei and was broken by it; the dead numbered in the tens of thousands.
idiomatic: Year twenty: Murong Bao attacked Wei and lost tens of thousands.

literal: In the twenty-first year, Chui died, and the state then declined to ruin.
idiomatic: Year twenty-one: Murong Chui died and Former Yan withered.

literal: In the twentieth year’s ninth month, there was a fuzzy star like powdered floss, moving southeast, passing Girl and Emptiness, reaching the Weeping star.
idiomatic: Year twenty, September: a misty broom drifted southeast through Girl-Void to the Weeping star.

literal: The prognostication states: "When a fuzzy star appears, within three years there must be a rebellious minister executed in the market."
idiomatic: Fuzzy stars within three years bring a traitor’s public execution.

literal: At the time Wang Guobao was weaving intrigues at court.
idiomatic: Wang Guobao was then poisoning court politics.

literal: In the twenty-first year’s ninth month, the emperor died.
idiomatic: Year twenty-one, September: the emperor died.

literal: In the first Long’an year, Wang Gong and others raised troops, and the court killed Wang Guobao and Wang Xu.
idiomatic: Long’an one: Wang Gong’s revolt prompted the court to kill Guobao and Xu.

literal: In Emperor An’s fourth Long’an year, second month, day Jichou, there was a star brooming in the Strider, three rods long, reaching up to the Forbidden Passage and the Purple Palace’s western bastion, entering the Dipper’s ladle, reaching the Three Steps; in the third month it then passed the Supreme Palace Enclosure’s imperial seat and Portal Gate.
idiomatic: Long’an four, jichou: a three-rod broom in Kui climbed to the Forbidden Passage, crossed the Purple Palace west wall and Dipper ladle, reached Three Steps, then in March swept the enclosure throne and Portal Gate.

literal: The prognostication states: "When a comet sweeps the Son of Heaven’s court and Forbidden Passage, it is an image of changing the ruler."
idiomatic: A comet brushing the court passage means a new sovereign.

literal: It passed the Three Steps and entered the Northern Dipper.
idiomatic: It crossed Three Steps into the Dipper.

literal: The prognostication was the same as the entry above.
idiomatic: Same gloss as the prior Three Steps–Dipper line.

literal: On day Wuyin in the twelfth month, there was a star brooming in the Coiled Rope, Celestial Market, and Celestial Ford.
idiomatic: December, wuyin: a broom through Coiled Rope, Market, and Ford.

literal: The prognostication states: "Noble ministers die in prison; inner and outer will have arms and mourning."
idiomatic: High officials perish in jail while war spreads inside and out.

literal: The Celestial Ford being cut by bandits means the royal way is blocked under Heaven.
idiomatic: When the Ford is severed, the king’s highway is choked.

literal: Investigating the prognostication: "The calamity lies in Wu and Yue."
idiomatic: Commentary pins the sign on Wu-Yue.

literal: In the fifth year’s second month, there was Sun En’s soldier rebellion, attacking and raiding commanderies and principalities.
idiomatic: Year five, February: Sun En’s mutiny ravaged the districts.

literal: Thereupon inner and outer were placed on alert; camps and formations garrisoned and held; palisades cut off the Huai mouth.
idiomatic: The realm locked down, armies walled the Huai crossings.

literal: In the ninth month, Huan Xuan’s memorial arrived, defying the decree and lording over the sovereign.
idiomatic: September: Huan Xuan’s arrogant memorial snubbed the throne.

literal: Afterward Xuan then usurped the throne, threw the capital into chaos, great famine set in, men ate one another, and the hundred surnames fled—all were its responses.
idiomatic: Huan Xuan seized power, starved Jiankang into cannibalism, and drove the people—all matching the omens.

literal: In the first Yuanxing year’s tenth month, there was a guest star, white like powdered floss, west of the Supreme Palace Enclosure, until the twelfth month it entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure.
idiomatic: Yuanxing one, October–December: a floss-white guest star slid from west of the enclosure into it.

literal: The prognostication states: "Arms enter the Son of Heaven’s court."
idiomatic: War enters the celestial court.

literal: In the second year’s twelfth month, Huan Xuan usurped the throne, banished emperor and empress to Xunyang, and made Empress He of Yong’an the Lady of Lingling.
idiomatic: Yuanxing two, December: Huan Xuan seized the throne and exiled the sovereigns.

literal: In the third year’s second month, Liu Yu exterminated the entire Huan clan.
idiomatic: Yuanxing three, February: Liu Yu wiped out the Huans.

literal: In the eleventh Yixi year, fifth month, day Jiashen, two comets issued from the Celestial Market, sweeping the imperial seat north of the Heart.
idiomatic: Yixi eleven, May, jiashen: twin comets from the Market brushed the throne north of the Heart.

literal: The Heart and Chamber are Song’s field allotment.
idiomatic: Heart-Chamber marks Song’s celestial territory.

literal: Investigating the prognostication: "He who gains the comet’s handle rises; removing the old and spreading the new is an image of Song’s rise."
idiomatic: Whoever catches the comet’s handle rises—an omen of Song’s founding.

literal: On day Gengzi in the fourteenth year’s fifth month, there was a star brooming inside the Northern Dipper’s ladle.
idiomatic: Yixi fourteen, May, gengzi: a broom inside the Dipper’s ladle.

literal: On day Guihai in the seventh month, a comet issued west of the Supreme Palace Enclosure, its handle rising below the senior minister star, its ray gradually lengthening to more than ten rods, advancing to sweep the Northern Dipper, Purple Tenuity, and the central Step.
idiomatic: July, guihai: a comet sprang west of the enclosure, handle under the senior minister, tail growing ten rods to brush Dipper, Purple Tenuity, and central Step.

literal: The prognostication states: "When a comet exits the Supreme Palace Enclosure, the altars of soil and grain perish and under Heaven the king changes;
idiomatic: A comet leaving the enclosure ends the dynasty and swaps the king;

literal: entering the Northern Dipper and Purple Tenuity means the imperial palace is empty."
idiomatic: piercing Dipper and Purple Tenuity empties the throne hall."

literal: In the fourteenth year, Liu Yu returned to Pengcheng and received the title Duke of Song.
idiomatic: Yixi fourteen: Liu Yu took the Song dukedom at Pengcheng.

literal: In the twelfth month, the emperor died.
idiomatic: December: the emperor died.

literal: In Emperor Gong’s first year, first month, day Wuxu, there was a star brooming on the Supreme Palace Enclosure’s western bastion.
idiomatic: Emperor Gong year one, first month, wuxu: a broom on the enclosure’s west wall.

literal: The prognostication states: "It is a sign of dynastic revolution."
idiomatic: Marks mandate revolution.

literal: That year, Song held all under Heaven.
idiomatic: That year Liu Song took the realm.

literal: Flowing stars and falling stars
idiomatic: Shooting stars and meteor falls

literal: Shu’s latter ruler: Zhuge Liang led a great host to campaign against Wei, encamping south of the Wei River.
idiomatic: Shu’s last king: Zhuge Liang massed an army against Wei on the Wei’s south bank.

literal: There was a long star, red with bristling rays, flowing from northeast to southwest, casting itself toward Liang’s camp, three times casting and twice returning, going large and returning small.
idiomatic: A long red meteor shot southwest toward Zhuge Liang’s camp, thrice striking and twice rebounding, swelling then shrinking.

literal: The prognostication states: "When two armies face each other, if a great shooting star runs onto the army or falls inside the army, all are signs of defeat and destruction."
idiomatic: Great meteors plunging into camps mean annihilation.

literal: In the ninth month, Liang died in the army; they burned the camp and withdrew; the various commanders turned on one another in blame, and many mutually slaughtered.
idiomatic: September: Zhuge Liang died in camp; Shu burned the lines; generals turned fratricidal.

literal: Wei Emperor Ming: the August Lord besieged Gongsun Wenyi at Xiangping.
idiomatic: Wei Mingdi: Sima Yi besieged Gongsun Yuan at Xiangping.

literal: On the night of day Bingyin in the eighth month, there was a great shooting star several tens of rods long, white with bristling mane, flowing from Shoushan northeast, falling southeast of Xiangping city.
idiomatic: August, bingyin night: a huge white meteor streaked from Shoushan into Xiangping’s southeast.

literal: The prognostication states: "When there is a siege and a shooting star runs onto the city or falls inside the city, it is broken."
idiomatic: Meteors striking a besieged city mean its fall.

literal: It also says: "Where a star falls, below it will be a battlefield."
idiomatic: A second gloss sets battle where the meteor lands.

literal: It also says: "In general wherever stars fall, the state changes surname."
idiomatic: A third gloss ties falls to dynastic change.

literal: In the ninth month, Wenyi broke the siege and fled; at the place the star fell he was beheaded; they slaughtered the city and buried its host in pits.
idiomatic: September: Gongsun Yuan fled to the fall site and died; Xiangping was sacked and its people massacred.

literal: In the sixth month of Yuan Di’s reign, there were two great shooting stars each like a dipper-ladle, seen in the west, dividing flow south and north, their light shining on the ground, rumbling with sound.
idiomatic: Jin Yuan emperor’s sixth month: twin dipper-sized western meteors split north and south, lighting the earth with thunder.

literal: Investigating the prognostication: "Shooting stars are noble envoys; when the star is large the envoy is great."
idiomatic: Meteors image great emissaries; larger stars mean greater men.

literal: That year, Zhong and Deng conquered Shu; the two stars were probably images of the two commanders.
idiomatic: That year Zhong Hui and Deng Ai took Shu—the twin meteors mirrored the two generals.

literal: The two commanders turned their backs on each other; it also matched dividing flow south and north.
idiomatic: Their mutual betrayal matched the split tails.

literal: After Zhong Hui rebelled, the three armies were furious; rumbling with sound is a sign of soldiers and generals angry.
idiomatic: When Zhong Hui mutinied, the hosts raged—the meteor’s roar imaged soldierly fury.

literal: In Emperor Wu’s seventh month, stars fell like rain, all flowing west.
idiomatic: Jin Wudi’s seventh month: a westward meteor shower.

literal: The prognostication states: "Star falls mean the hundred surnames rebel."
idiomatic: Meteor showers mean popular revolt.

literal: Flowing west is an image of Wu people submitting to Jin."
idiomatic: Westward flow showed Wu yielding to Jin."

literal: In the second year, Wu’s Xiakou commander Sun Xiu led more than two thousand households of troops to surrender.
idiomatic: Year two: Wu’s Sun Xiu brought two thousand families over.

literal: On day Renzi in the eighth month, stars fell like rain.
idiomatic: August, renzi: another meteor rain.

literal: Liu Xiang’s "Tradition" states: "It is an image of the lower displacing the upper."
idiomatic: Liu Xiang reads it as inferiors overturning superiors.

literal: After three years the emperor died and Emperor Hui was established; under Heaven from this was chaotic.
idiomatic: Three years on the emperor died, Hui succeeded, and chaos engulfed the realm.

literal: In Emperor Hui’s ninth month, day Jiawu, a crooked arrow went northeast, spanning the sky.
idiomatic: Huidi, September, jiawu: a crooked-arrow comet stretched northeast across the sky.

literal: On the night of day Bingwu in the sixth year’s sixth month, there was a crooked arrow from the Dipper’s ladle moving southeast.
idiomatic: Year six, June, bingwu night: a crooked arrow left the Dipper southeastward.

literal: Investigating, the prognostication states: "Using disorder to attack disorder."
idiomatic: Commentary: chaos fights chaos.

literal: The Northern Dipper governs executions and killing; issuing from the Dipper’s ladle, the executioner in the center not being straight is an image."
idiomatic: The Dipper rules killing; a crooked arrow from its ladle marks unjust executioners."

literal: Afterward Prince Zhao killed Zhang and Pei, deposed Empress Jia to redress the heir’s grievance, then himself usurped and stole, down to extermination—responses to using disorder to attack disorder.
idiomatic: Then Sima Lun killed Zhang and Pei, toppled Empress Jia for the crown prince, then seized power and was destroyed—chaos answering chaos.

literal: One gloss says: it was also the response to Di chieftain Qi Wannian’s rebellion.
idiomatic: Another line ties the sign to Qi Wannian’s Di revolt.

literal: On day Xinsi in the eleventh month, there was a star that fell in daytime from mid-sky to the north, its light turning white, with sound like thunder.
idiomatic: November, xinsi: a daytime fireball dropped northward, flashed white, and thundered.

literal: Investigating the prognostication: "Its name is Camp Head."
idiomatic: The books call it a Camp Head meteor.

literal: Where Camp Head lies, below there will be a great army and flowing blood."
idiomatic: Under Camp Head falls great slaughter."

literal: The next year, Liu Yuan and Shi Le raided Bing Province, greatly destroying it.
idiomatic: Next year Liu Yuan and Shi Le ravaged Bingzhou.

literal: Wang Jun rose in Yan and Dai, leading Xianbei to raid Ye, and the hundred surnames were smeared on the ground.
idiomatic: Wang Jun mobilized Yan-Dai Xianbei to scour Ye and trample the people.

literal: Having sound like thunder is an image of anger.
idiomatic: Thunderous noise images wrath.

literal: On day Yichou in the seventh month, stars fell with sound.
idiomatic: July, yichou: noisy meteors.

literal: In the second year’s tenth month, stars again fell with sound.
idiomatic: Year two, October: more sounding meteors.

literal: The prognostication was the same as above.
idiomatic: Same meteor gloss.

literal: Afterward, the central plain was then lost.
idiomatic: The heartland was lost soon after.

literal: In the fifth month, a crooked arrow flowed southwest.
idiomatic: May: a crooked-arrow comet ran southwest.

literal: At the time Sima Yue broke the Hejian army in the west, welcomed the great chariot, then seized Miao Yin, He Sui, and others, wantonly showing lack of fealty to the ruler; under Heaven hated him.
idiomatic: Sima Yue crushed Hejian, escorted the emperor, then arrested Miao Yin and He Sui, flaunting disloyalty until the realm despised him.

literal: When he died, Shi Le burned his coffin; this was its response.
idiomatic: Shi Le burned Yue’s bier—matching the omen.

literal: In Emperor Huai’s ninth month, day Xinmao, there was a great star like the sun, flowing from southwest to northeast, small ones like dippers following, the whole sky turning red, sound like thunder.
idiomatic: Huaidi, September, xinmao: a sun-bright bolide crossed the sky with dipper-sized followers, reddening the heavens with thunder.

literal: The prognostication states: "Shooting stars are noble envoys; when the star is large the envoy is great."
idiomatic: Large meteors image great agents of fate.

literal: That year’s fifth month, Ji Sang killed Prince Teng of Eastern Yan and then held the Yellow River’s north.
idiomatic: That May Ji Sang slew Prince Teng and seized north Hebei.

literal: In the eleventh month, they first dispatched He Yu as General Who Conquers the North, garrisoning west of Ye.
idiomatic: November: He Yu was sent to camp west of Ye.

literal: Tian Zhen and others greatly broke Ji Sang and beheaded him at Leling.
idiomatic: Tian Zhen shattered Ji Sang and took his head at Leling.

literal: Thereupon Zhen was made governor of Ji commandery and his younger brother Lan governor of Julu.
idiomatic: Tian Zhen became Ji governor; his brother Lan Julu governor.

literal: Small stars following mean images of minor generals and separate commanders.
idiomatic: Trailing small meteors mark subordinate columns.

literal: Sima Yue resented that east of Wei commandery and south of Pingyuan all sided with Sang, and rewarded Zhen and others, thereupon raiding until the land was bare.
idiomatic: Yue, furious that Wei east and Pingyuan south backed Sang, rewarded Tian Zhen’s raids until the soil was scorched bare.

literal: Having sound like thunder is an image of wrath.
idiomatic: Thunder again signals rage.

literal: On day Gengzi in the fourth year’s tenth month, a great star fell northwest with sound.
idiomatic: Year four, October, gengzi: a huge northwest meteor boomed.

literal: Soon the emperor was dust-smirched at Pingyang.
idiomatic: Soon the emperor suffered captivity at Pingyang.

literal: In Yuan Di’s fourth month, day Renchen, a crooked arrow issued from Emptiness and Rooftops and sank in Wings and Chariot.
idiomatic: Jin Yuan emperor, April, renchen: a crooked arrow ran Void-Rooftops to Wings-Chariot.

literal: The prognostication states: "What the crooked arrow strikes is what under Heaven punishes."
idiomatic: The crooked arrow marks heaven’s target.

literal: Wings and Chariot are Jing Province’s field allotment.
idiomatic: Wings-Chariot map to Jingzhou.

literal: Wang Dun killed Prince Cheng of Qiao and Gan Zhuo, and Dun was then executed and displayed; it was the response of the crooked arrow touching the Wings.
idiomatic: Wang Dun slew Sima Cheng and Gan Zhuo, then died himself—the arrow’s touch on Wings fulfilled.

literal: On day Jiawu in the seventh month, there was a shooting star large as a vat, more than a hundred rods long, bluish red, coming from the west, its tail dividing into more than a hundred forks, some scattering.
idiomatic: July, jiawu: a vat-sized western meteor split into a hundred tails.

literal: It was the response to Wang Dun’s rebellion and the hundred surnames fleeing in exile.
idiomatic: It answered Wang Dun’s revolt and the people’s flight.

literal: In Emperor Cheng’s first month, day Xinwei, there was a shooting star large as two dipper-ladles, bluish red, its light shining on the ground, issuing from within the Strider, sinking north of Bond.
idiomatic: Emperor Cheng’s first month, xinwei: a twin-dipper meteor blazed from Kui to north Bond.
